events.title: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem
events.shortBlurb: After a five-week siege the armies of the First Crusade took the Holy City, the goal proclaimed at Clermont four years before…
body: Summoned by Pope Urban II at Clermont in November 1095, the armies of the First Crusade reached Jerusalem in June 1099, reduced by three years of marching and battle to perhaps thirteen thousand fighting men. The city, held by the Fatimids of Egypt, was invested on 7 June amid summer heat and thirst.

On 15 July 1099, after five weeks of siege, the crusaders breached the northern wall near the siege tower of Godfrey of Bouillon and poured into the city. The sack that followed was merciless: Muslims and Jews alike were massacred in numbers the chroniclers reckoned in the tens of thousands, a butchery the victors themselves recorded without shame.

A week later Godfrey of Bouillon was chosen ruler of the conquered city, refusing the name of king and taking instead the title Advocate of the Holy Sepulchre. Thus was founded the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem, which endured until Saladin's victory at Hattin in 1187, while the last crusader foothold in the East, Acre, survived until 1291.

events.title: The death of St. Bonaventure at Lyons
events.shortBlurb: The Seraphic Doctor died during the Second Council of Lyons he had helped to guide…
body: Gregory X had called the fourteenth general council to Lyons to succor the Holy Land, reform Christian life, and end the Greek schism; it opened on 7 May 1274 with the pope himself presiding. Thomas Aquinas died on the road to the council, at Fossanova that March, and it fell to Bonaventure, Cardinal-Bishop of Albano, to prepare the agenda and conduct the conferences with the Greek envoys.

The union was sealed on 6 July, when the Greek confession of faith was read and accepted in the pope's presence. Nine days later, on 15 July, Bonaventure died suddenly; the chronicle of his secretary alleged poison, but the cause cannot now be known. He was buried the next evening in the Franciscan church at Lyons, with the pope, the King of Aragon, and the council fathers at his funeral.

The council closed on 17 July, and the reunion it acclaimed was cast off at Constantinople within the decade. Bonaventure's relics fared ill — the Huguenots burned his body in the public square in 1562, and the head then rescued was lost in the French Revolution. Lyons had chosen him for a patron when his remains were found incorrupt in 1434.
